page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom-quartile scores in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth falls into the bottom 25%. Cryptographic operations perform moderately well, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets, though database operations and static web serving throughput remain in the lower performance tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-4 offers a dedicated hardware profile suitable for workloads that require consistent single-threaded performance without the overhead of shared-core environments. Given its moderate memory-to-vCPU ratio and lower multi-core efficiency, it is best suited for light single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-concurrency web serving. It is less optimal for highly parallelized tasks, large database management, or memory-intensive compilation jobs.
